symptoms.question: Is the brake warning light on (or does it say brake)? (yes/no)
Does the brake pedal feel unusually soft or go closer to the floor? (yes/no)
Do you hear squealing noises when braking? (yes/no)
Do you hear grinding noises when braking? (yes/no)
Does the car pull to one side when braking? (yes/no)

rules.diagnosis: Brake warning light with a soft pedal suggests a hydraulic brake issue (fluid leak or air in system).
rules.advice: Do not continue driving. Braking performance may be severely reduced. Call for assistance or have the car towed.

rules.diagnosis: Squealing when braking often indicates worn brake pads.
rules.advice: Drive gently and book a brake inspection soon to avoid damage to discs.

rules.diagnosis: Grinding noise when braking can indicate pads are worn through and metal is contacting the disc.
rules.advice: Stop driving if possible and have the brakes repaired immediately to prevent loss of braking and expensive damage.

rules.diagnosis: Pulling to one side under braking can indicate uneven braking force (caliper issue, fluid issue, or worn components).
rules.advice: Reduce speed and book an inspection soon. If pulling becomes severe, stop driving.

rules.diagnosis: Brake warning light can indicate low brake fluid, parking brake issue, or other brake system problem.
rules.advice: Check brake fluid level if safe. If the warning persists, avoid driving and have the brakes checked urgently.
